title.narrative: Operational budget for ICD681 to track CAFOD’s operational costs

description.narrative:
This project will contribute towards enabling the communities in the targeted areas of Mollo (Lozhu payam), Larugura (Kediba payam) and Lakamadi (Lakamadi payam) within the Catholic Diocese of Yei to live together in a safe and clean environment with dignity. This will be achieved through the promotion and support of good hygiene and sanitation practices in the communities. Communities will be supported to construct 100 low cost household latrines which will directly benefit 100 Households (700 individuals) and taught how to practice good sanitation and hygiene that will lead to a reduction in open defecation and a reduction in incidences of hygiene/water borne related diseases. The use of media in disseminating good hygiene practices will highly be adopted with frequent radio talk shows on good hygiene practices as well as short radio spot messages on hygiene. This project will build on the 2012/2013 water, sanitation and hygiene project activities as well as the 2013 community sanitation project that CAFOD and the diocese of Yei implemented with funding from Caritas Australia and CAFOD.
Beneficiary selection criteria will be developed and part of the criteria will include willingness for participation of selected households to dig the pits and provide manual labour to support in the construction of the latrines, rather than engaging external private construction companies. Besides supporting the community to construct low cost pit latrines, communities will also be trained by the community hygiene promoters on the use of the latrines and on hygiene and sanitation related good practices including use of hand washing facilities at the latrine points.
The targeting of beneficiaries will be done is such a way that the most vulnerable and marginalised members of the communities will be given priority. A poverty and vulnerability ranking system that takes into consideration the economic status, disability status, socio status such as women headed, child headed households and households with chronically ill and elderly members will be used through community based group discussions. Households will be ranked based on this criterion with the most vulnerable being selected to be beneficiaries. This will be done in collaboration with local government authorities such as the Department of Rural Water and Sanitation which participated during assessments, data analysis, design of activities, and supervision of the construction work to the latrines. This project is therefore created for Operational budget for CAFOD,s staff to track CAFOD’s operational costs.
